name: Sibyl's Drift

stars.name: Sibyl
stars.notes: Ancient flare-prone red dwarf; its slow, sullen flicker gives the system its funereal character.

stars.name: Necra
stars.notes: White dwarf remnant of the system's original primary; its metal-polluted spectrum shows it is still consuming planetary debris.

planets.name: Lethes
planets.notes: Radiation-scoured cinder skimming both stellar winds; probes last minutes on its surface.

planets.name: Vellum
planets.notes: Pale sedimentary world scored with channels; erosion patterns resemble lines of script, unsettling survey crews.

planets.name: Codex
planets.notes: Cracked ice shell over a dead ocean; strata preserve layered dust falls in pages-like bands.

planets.name: Palimpsest
planets.notes: Airless world bearing the erased ruins of a forgotten empire: foundations scraped flat, monuments defaced, then overwritten by newer structures of alien geometry.

anomalies.name: The Quill of Hours
anomalies.notes: Time slips near the white dwarf replay moments of the system's past; instruments have recorded landings that have not yet occurred.

anomalies.name: Ledger of Tomorrows
anomalies.notes: Weak temporal gradient where sensors intermittently register readings dated days ahead; expeditions anchor to it at their peril.

asteroid_belts.name: Marginalia Belt
asteroid_belts.notes: Thin debris ring feeding Necra's accretion; occasional fragments fall inward trailing glowing tails.

faction_control.notes: No power holds the system; several archival guilds maintain overlapping claims they decline to enforce.

history: Flagged during a white dwarf debris survey when automated probes logged sensor returns timestamped in the future.
The first manned expedition found Palimpsest's erased ruins and confirmed the echo loops, recording a lander's arrival weeks before it touched down.
Successive study missions ended in disappearances; the system now draws only solitary archivists and foolhardy treasure seekers.
description: Sibyl's Drift is a dying binary: a feeble red dwarf wheeling a hungry white dwarf whose blue glare picks over the wreckage of former worlds. Four thin planets circle the pair in wide circumbinary paths, their surfaces scoured by nine billion years of stellar decay.

Nothing lives here, yet the system is never entirely empty. Archivists drift through on minimal traffic, chasing the twin temporal anomalies that smear cause behind effect and leak readings from tomorrow. On Palimpsest, the ruins of a forgotten empire lie scraped and rewritten like a reused scroll, evidence of a civilization that flourished and was deliberately erased.

The mysteries compound with each visit. Who effaced Palimpsest's monuments, and why build anew atop the rubble? Do the echo loops preserve the empire's final days, and could the Ledger of Tomorrows be made to yield them? Those who linger too long report meeting themselves in the dust, and some never report anything again.
